claim: Tool execution, not LLM generation, is the dominant latency bottleneck in agent workloads, accounting for 60% of latency in coding tasks, 50% in deep research tasks, and 36% in scientific tasks across three mainstream agent benchmarks.
stance_target: motivation for building probabilistic tool/skill-sequence prediction systems
scope_conditions: Deep Research Bench, SWE-bench, ScholarQA benchmarks; Gemini-2.5, GPT-5.2, Qwen-DeepResearch-30B
quoted_support: On average, tool execution accounts for 60% of the latency in coding tasks, 50% in deep research tasks, and 36% in scientific tasks.

claim: Agent tool-call sequences exhibit strong, measurable control-flow regularities that can be mined from historical traces: 55% of file_editor write/replace calls are immediately followed by a pytest/python terminal call (Edit-Verify pattern), and 38% of grep calls are immediately followed by file_editor (Locate-Examine pattern).
stance_target: probabilistic skill-sequence prediction from agent-trace history is empirically grounded in coding-agent workflows
scope_conditions: coding/bug-fix agent traces from SWE-bench, MetaGPT, OpenHands
quoted_support: Among all coding traces, 55% of successful file_editor tool calls (write/replace) were immediately followed by a terminal tool call (specifically pytest or python execution)... Among all coding traces, 38% of grep tool calls were immediately followed by file_editor tool call.

claim: The Pattern Tuple abstraction (context, prediction, function, probability) decouples skill/tool control-flow prediction from data-flow (argument) prediction, using event signatures over tool types rather than natural-language phrasing, making prediction robust to the semantic diversity of user requests.
stance_target: architecture design for probabilistic skill-sequence prediction systems
quoted_support: the tuple defines context strictly over event signatures (sequences of tool types), allowing the system to identify stable control flows amidst volatile user inputs... the tuple utilizes a symbolic value mapping function to encode the logical relationships between data, enabling the system to automatically resolve implicit parameter passing between tools without invoking the LLM.

claim: A probabilistic next-tool predictor with only 27.8% top-1 accuracy can still deliver large end-to-end speedups if paired with top-3 recall of 43.9% and an overall speculative hit rate of 93.8%, because the scheduler can speculatively execute multiple ranked candidates within a bounded resource budget.
stance_target: imperfect probabilistic prediction is still practically useful for skill-chaining systems if ranked-candidate coverage is high
scope_conditions: VirtualLab, Qwen Deep Research, gemini-cli agents on DeepResearchBench, SWE-bench, ScholarQA
quoted_support: Overall, the predictor achieves up to 27.8% Top-1 accuracy, 43.9% Top-3 recall, and 93.8% overall hit rate... Despite imperfect Top-1 accuracy, strong Top-3 recall is sufficient in practice: PASTE can speculate on a small set of likely tools and still obtain overlap when any candidate hits.

claim: PASTE's risk-aware opportunistic scheduler, which runs speculative (predicted) skill/tool invocations only on transient idle resource slack and instantly preempts on contention, achieves a measured 48.5% average end-to-end latency reduction and 1.25x/1.32x speedup over ORION/SpecFaaS baselines without altering task outputs.
stance_target: a probabilistic skill-chaining system can deliver large measured production speedups while preserving correctness
scope_conditions: 4-node cluster, 32x NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, Azure Functions real trace-driven arrivals; VirtualLab, Qwen Deep Research, gemini-cli agents
quoted_support: PASTE reduces average latency by up to 48.5%, and reduces p95/p99 tail latency by up to 48.6%/61.9%. Aggregating across all configurations, PASTE achieves an average speedup of 1.25x/1.32x over ORION/SpecFaaS.

claim: Speculative execution of probabilistically predicted tool calls carries real side-effect risk requiring active safeguarding: an audit found 602 potentially side-effecting speculative actions among over 20,000 total speculative actions, all successfully blocked from committing before authoritative confirmation.
stance_target: risk management requirements for autonomous probabilistic skill/tool pre-execution
scope_conditions: all evaluated workloads (VirtualLab, Qwen Deep Research, gemini-cli)
quoted_support: PASTE detects 602 potentially side-effecting speculative actions among over 20,000 speculative actions and prevents them from committing. No task produces a different final result compared with the baselines.

claim: Prior static-DAG-based serverless speculation systems (ORION, SpecFaaS) are ineffective for agentic workloads because agent control flow is generated online per-step and the next tool call is unknown until the LLM finishes the current reasoning step, unlike systems with a complete execution graph a priori.
stance_target: static workflow/DAG-based prediction approaches are sufficient for skill-sequence prediction in autonomous agents
quoted_support: This assumption breaks for agentic workloads: the control flow is generated online, and the next tool call is not known until the LLM finishes the current step. Without the full DAG a priori, ahead-of-time scheduling and graph-based prefetching provide limited benefit.
